title: Rohit Sharma 'Plays' for Pakistan in Viral Broadcast Blunder
excerpt: A graphics mix-up at the BAN vs PAK Test in Dhaka accidentally displayed India's full playing XI under Pakistan's flag.
body:
Cricket fans watching the first Test between Bangladesh and Pakistan in Dhaka on May 9 got far more than they bargained for — India's entire playing XI appeared on screen under the Pakistan flag, in one of the most viral broadcast blunders in recent memory.

**What happened on Day 2:**
Just after Pakistan captain Shan Masood won the toss and elected to field at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium, the production team flashed a graphic meant to show Pakistan's Playing XI. Instead, viewers saw a full India scorecard listing Rohit Sharma as captain, alongside Shubman Gill, Tilak Varma, Shivam Dube, Jitesh Sharma, Rinku Singh, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Ravi Bishnoi, Arshdeep Singh, and Mukesh Kumar — none of whom were anywhere near Dhaka. The likely culprit was a wrong graphic template loaded during the live telecast.

**Why cricket Twitter couldn't stop laughing:**
Screenshots spread within minutes, and the meme festival began. Fans joked that 'India lives rent free' in the Pakistan production team's minds, while others questioned how such a basic quality check fails during an international Test broadcast. The official broadcasters have not issued any statement or explanation. Meanwhile, on the field, Bangladesh quietly dominated — posting a formidable 413 in their first innings, anchored by captain Najmul Hossain Shanto's rapid 101, Mominul Haque's 91, and Mushfiqur Rahim's gritty 71.

**What to watch next:**
All eyes now shift to whether Pakistan's depleted batting lineup — missing Babar Azam due to injury — can fight back against Bangladesh's pace attack led by Taskin Ahmed and Nahid Rana, and whether the broadcasters issue a formal explanation for the on-air gaffe.
